products.name: Quote to Buy — Home Insurance
products.description: End-to-end quote and purchase flow for home insurance

tasks: Get a quote for home insurance with standard details
Update your excess amount and see the new price
Find and understand what events are not covered
Complete the purchase with a saved payment method
testPlan.notes: Same 4 tasks every round. Do NOT change tasks between rounds — longitudinal consistency is required for valid comparison.

rounds.label: Baseline (pre-redesign)
rounds.notes: Baseline before progress bar redesign. Major friction at address confirmation (stage 3).
significantFindings: 34% drop-off at vehicle details — empty form with no pre-fill
Average 10+ clicks before seeing a price
3/42 participants called RAA instead of completing online

rounds.label: Post-redesign (progress bar + pre-fill)
rounds.notes: Progress bar and pre-fill both shipped. Significant improvement across all metrics.
significantFindings: Task completion up 16 percentage points (statistically significant, p < 0.01)
Pre-fill eliminated the empty form problem — drop-off at stage 3 fell from 34% to 12%

rounds.label: Quarterly drift check
rounds.notes: Slight regression from R2. New payment method selector may be causing confusion. Investigating.
significantFindings: Task completion dropped 3pp from R2 — not statistically significant (within CI overlap)
Error rate increased slightly — 2 participants confused by new payment selector

chromeScans.label: Pre-redesign baseline scan
findings: Address confirmation mismatch between entered and displayed format
Calculator opens in new tab — breaks flow
No pre-fill on vehicle details despite data existing in policy system

newFeatures: Pre-filled vehicle details from policy system
newFrictions: Payment method selector has small tap targets on mobile

screensAdded: New payment method selection screen (added by dev without design review)
newFrictions: New payment screen adds a step
Payment method selector layout differs from design spec

products.name: My Account — Policy Management
products.description: Viewing and managing existing policies, updating details, and accessing documents

tasks: Find your current home insurance policy and check the renewal date
Update your address on an existing policy
Add a second driver to your motor policy
testPlan.notes: Baseline only — no redesign delivered yet.

rounds.label: Baseline
rounds.notes: Very poor baseline. Navigation is the primary issue — participants cannot find their policies.
significantFindings: Average time on task over 6.5 minutes
12/36 participants used search instead of navigation — search returned no results for 'policy'

chromeScans.label: Baseline scan
findings: 22 screens across policy management — no clear hierarchy
Search returns no results for common terms like 'policy' and 'renewal'
Certificate download requires: My Account → Policies → Select → Documents → Certificate → Download (6 clicks)
Address update form clears all fields on validation error
No confirmation step before address change is saved

products.name: Taskly — Onboarding Flow
products.description: New user registration and first-task creation flow for the Taskly demo app

tasks: Create a new account using your email
Set up your first project and give it a name
Create a task with a due date and assign it to yourself
Find the task you just created and mark it complete
testPlan.notes: Demo product — faster iteration cycle than production RAA products.

rounds.label: V1 — basic flow
rounds.notes: Good baseline for a new product. Date picker was the main confusion point.
significantFindings: Date picker caused 8/30 participants to enter wrong format
Task creation was intuitive — 28/30 completed without help
3 participants expected a tutorial/walkthrough on first login

rounds.label: V2 — improved date picker + onboarding tooltip
rounds.notes: Significant improvement. Date picker fix resolved the main error source. Onboarding tooltip helped first-time users.
significantFindings: Error rate dropped from 12% to 5% — date picker fix confirmed
Time on task reduced 19% — onboarding tooltip saved exploration time

uxBenchmarking.description: Quantitative usability testing with fixed tasks, run at regular intervals to measure change over time.
rules: Same tasks every round — never change the test between rounds
Same participant criteria — demographics, tech proficiency, familiarity with product
Same platform and test conditions — moderated vs unmoderated stays consistent
Minimum 30 participants per round for statistical significance
Report confidence intervals (95% CI) for all metrics
Statistical significance tested between rounds — p < 0.05 minimum

taskCompletion.name: Task Completion Rate
taskCompletion.description: Percentage of participants who complete all tasks successfully

timeOnTask.name: Time on Task
timeOnTask.description: Average time to complete the task set

errorRate.name: Error Rate
errorRate.description: Percentage of participants who encounter at least one error

chromeScanning.description: Automated product state capture using Claude's Chrome extension. Documents every screen, form field, and interaction point.

metrics.totalScreens: Number of distinct screens in the flow
metrics.totalFormFields: Total form inputs across all screens
metrics.totalClicks: Minimum clicks to complete the primary task

chromeScanning.cadence: Before and after each delivery cycle, plus quarterly drift checks

statisticalNotes.confidenceInterval: All metrics report 95% confidence intervals. If the CIs of two rounds overlap, the difference is likely not statistically significant.
statisticalNotes.sampleSize: Minimum 30 participants per round. Below 30, confidence intervals widen and results become unreliable for decision-making.
statisticalNotes.significance: We use p < 0.05 as the threshold. A result is 'statistically significant' when there's less than a 5% chance the difference is due to random variation.
statisticalNotes.longitudinal: Benchmarking studies are longitudinal by definition. Changing the tasks, participant criteria, or test conditions between rounds invalidates the comparison. If the product changes enough that the tasks no longer make sense, start a new benchmark study — don't modify the existing one.
